mathFunction.title: Math Functions
mathFunction.absDescDetail: Calculates the absolute value of one number
mathFunction.averageDescDetail: Calculates the arithmetic mean of a group of numbers. Empty fields are ignored
mathFunction.averageColumnDescDetail: Calculates the arithmetic mean of the full column for specified fields in a form. Empty fields are ignored
mathFunction.averageColumnExample: AVERAGECOLUMN(Student Scores. Chinese Score, Student Scores. Math Score)calculates the average of Chinese Score and Math Score in the Student Scores form
mathFunction.ceilingDesc: Round up to a multiple of the specified base
mathFunction.ceilingDescDetail: Rounds a number up to the nearest integer multiple of the base
mathFunction.ceilingExample: CEILING(5, 4)returns the integer greater than 5 that is closest to 5 and is a multiple of 4. The result is 8
mathFunction.countDescDetail: Counts non-empty rows of number/date fields in subforms or query forms, or counts non-empty fields among multiple number/date fields in the main form
mathFunction.countSyntax:
COUNT(Query Form.Number/Date Field)
COUNT([Number Field1, Date Field2, ..., Number/Date FieldN])
mathFunction.countExample:
Query form example: COUNT(Query Form-Sales. Contract Amount), counts records whose Contract Amount is not empty in the Sales query form
Multiple main-form fields example: COUNT([Expense Request. Monthly Budget, Expense Request. Actual Spend, Expense Request. Project Start Date]), If the current Expense Request record has Monthly Budget=5000, Actual Spend empty, and Project Start Date=2024-01-15, the count result is 2'
mathFunction.countADescDetail: Counts non-empty rows of specified single-value fields in subforms or query forms, or counts non-empty fields among multiple single-value fields
mathFunction.countASyntax:
COUNTA(Query Form.Single-value Field)
COUNTA([Single-value Field1, Single-value Field2, ..., Single-value FieldN])
mathFunction.countAExample:
Query form example: COUNTA(Query Form-Personnel. Phone), counts records whose Phone field is not empty in the Personnel query form
Multiple main-form fields example: COUNTA([Quiz. Single Choice 1, Quiz. Single Choice 2, Quiz. Single Choice 3]), If Single Choice 1 and 2 have answers in the Quiz main form but Single Choice 3 has no answer, only Single Choice 1 and 2 are non-empty. The final count is 2'
mathFunction.countBlankDescDetail: Counts empty rows of specified single-value fields in subforms or query forms, or counts empty fields among multiple single-value fields
mathFunction.countBlankSyntax:
COUNTBLANK(Query Form.Single-value Field)
COUNTBLANK([Single-value Field1, Single-value Field2, ..., Single-value FieldN])
mathFunction.countBlankExample:
Query form example: COUNTBLANK(Query Form-Personnel. Phone), counts records whose Phone field is empty in the Personnel query form
Multiple main-form fields example: COUNTBLANK([Quiz. Single Choice 1, Quiz. Single Choice 2, Quiz. Single Choice 3]), If Single Choice 1 and 2 have answers in the Quiz main form but Single Choice 3 has no answer, only Single Choice 3 is empty. The final count is 1'
mathFunction.countIfDescDetail: Counts parameters in an array that meet the condition
mathFunction.countIfExample: COUNTIF([1, 3, 5, 7], ">=3") counts numbers greater than or equal to 3 in the array. The result is 3\n COUNTIF(Sales. Contract Amount, ">10000") counts rows in the Sales subform where Contract Amount is greater than 10000
mathFunction.countIfsDescDetail: Counts parameters in an array that meet multiple conditions
mathFunction.countIfsExample: COUNTIFS(Sales. Contract Amount, ">10000", Sales. Contract Status, "Signed") counts rows in the Sales subform where Contract Amount is greater than 10000 and Contract Status is Signed
mathFunction.fixedDescDetail: Rounds by specified decimal places. If decimal places are omitted or 0, returns an integer. Also supports converting the result to text
mathFunction.fixedExample: FIXED(1. 5678, 2), If returning a number, the result is 1. 57. If returning text, the result is 2
mathFunction.floorDesc: Rounds the number down to the nearest specified multiple
mathFunction.floorExample: FLOOR(7, 2)returns the integer less than 7 that is closest to 7 and is a multiple of 2. The result is 6
mathFunction.intDescDetail: Drops the decimal part of a number and returns an integer
mathFunction.largeDescDetail: Returns the X-th largest value in an array
mathFunction.largeExample:
LARGE([1, 3, 5, 7], 2)gets the 2nd largest value in the array. The result is 5
LARGE(Sales. Contract Amount, 1)gets the 1st ranked Contract Amount in the Sales subform
mathFunction.largeColumnDesc: Get maximum from a specified form column
mathFunction.largeColumnDescDetail: Returns the X-th largest value in the full column of a specified field in a form
mathFunction.largeColumnExample:
LARGECOLUMN(Form Field, 2)gets the 2nd largest value from the full column of the specified field. The result is 5
LARGECOLUMN(Student Scores. Chinese Score, 1)gets the 1st ranked Chinese Score in the Student Scores form
mathFunction.logDescDetail: Returns the logarithm of a number using the specified base
mathFunction.logExample: LOG(100, 10)calculates the logarithm of 100 with base 10. The result is 2
mathFunction.maxDescDetail: Returns the maximum value from a group of numbers
mathFunction.maxExample: MAX(Sales1, Sales2, Sales3)returns the maximum among the three sales values
mathFunction.minDescDetail: Returns the minimum value from a group of numbers
mathFunction.minExample: MIN(Sales1, Sales2, Sales3)returns the minimum among the three sales values
mathFunction.modDescDetail: Calculates the remainder after dividing two numbers
mathFunction.modExample: MOD(7, 3)is the remainder of 7/3. The result is 1
mathFunction.powerDescDetail: Calculates the power of a number
mathFunction.powerExample: POWER(2, 3)is 2 to the 3rd power. The result is 8
mathFunction.productDescDetail: Calculates the result of multiplying multiple numbers
mathFunction.productExample: PRODUCT(Sales Volume, Unit Price)returns Sales Volume x Unit Price as total sales amount
mathFunction.roundDescDetail: Rounds a number to the specified decimal places
mathFunction.roundExample: ROUND(1. 5789, 2)rounds to two decimal places. The result is 1. 58
mathFunction.roundDownDescDetail: Rounds a number down toward zero
mathFunction.roundDownExample:
ROUNDDOWN(3. 3, 0)rounds 3. 3 down to zero decimal places. The result is 3
ROUNDDOWN(-5. 24133, 1)rounds -5. 24133 down to one decimal place. The result is -5. 2
mathFunction.smallDescDetail: Returns the X-th smallest value in an array
mathFunction.smallExample:
SMALL([1, 3, 5, 7], 2)gets the 2nd smallest value in the array. The result is 3
SMALL(Sales. Contract Amount, 1)gets the smallest Contract Amount in the Sales subform
mathFunction.smallColumnDesc: Get minimum from a specified form column
mathFunction.smallColumnDescDetail: Returns the X-th smallest value in the full column of a specified field in a form
mathFunction.smallColumnExample:
SMALLCOLUMN(Form Field, 2)gets the 2nd smallest value from the full column of the specified field. The result is 3
SMALLCOLUMN(Student Scores. Chinese Score, 1)gets the smallest Chinese Score in the Student Scores form
mathFunction.sqrtDescDetail: Calculates the positive square root of a number
mathFunction.sqrtExample: SQRT(4)is the positive square root of 4. The result is 2
mathFunction.sumDescDetail: Calculates the result of adding multiple numbers
mathFunction.sumExample: SUM(Sales1, Sales2, Sales3)returns the sum of the three sales values
mathFunction.sumColumnDescDetail: Calculates the sum of full-column data for specified fields in a form
mathFunction.sumColumnExample: SUMCOLUMN(Travel Expenses. Transport, Travel Expenses. Accommodation, Travel Expenses. Meals) returns the total of all travel expenses
mathFunction.sumProductDescDetail: Multiplies corresponding elements across arrays and returns the sum of products
mathFunction.sumIfDesc: Sum values in a range that meet a condition
mathFunction.sumIfDescDetail: Adds numbers in a range that meet the specified condition and returns the sum.
mathFunction.sumIfSyntax: SUMIF(Criteria Range, logical expression, Sum Range)
mathFunction.sumIfExample: SUMIF(Subform. Product Type, "Banana", Subform. Number), sums the corresponding numbers where Product Type is Banana in the subform; SUMIF([D, B, C, C, A], "A", [1, 1, 1, 1, 1]), returns the sum for type C as 2; SUMIF(Subform. Score, ">=60", Subform. Credits)
mathFunction.sumIfsDescDetail: Adds numbers that meet multiple conditions and returns the sum.
mathFunction.sumIfsSyntax: SUMIFS(Array_Sum Range, Array_Criteria Range1, Logical Expression1, Array_Criteria Range2, Logical Expression2, .. .)
mathFunction.sumIfsExample: SUMIFS(Subform. Number, Subform. Product Type, "Banana", Subform. Subcategory, "Imported"), sums corresponding numbers where Product Type is Banana and Subcategory is Imported in the subform; SUMIFS(Subform. Sales Amount, Subform. Salesperson, "John", Subform. Sales Region, "East China", Subform. Product Category, "Mobile Phone")

textFunction.title: Text Functions
textFunction.charDescDtl: Converts a number to the corresponding computer character
textFunction.concatDescDtl: Merges multiple text values into one text value
textFunction.concatExample: CONCATENATE("Today", "weather", "is nice")merges three text values. The result is "Todayweatheris nice"
textFunction.exactDescDtl: Compares whether two text values are exactly the same. Returns true if same, otherwise false
textFunction.exactExample: EXACT(Lottery Number, Winning Lottery Number), returns true if the two numbers match, otherwise false
textFunction.joinDescDtl: Joins array values into one text value with a separator
textFunction.leftDesc: Return specified characters from the left
textFunction.leftDescDtl: Returns a specified number of characters from the first character on the left of a text value. If the text is shorter, returns the original text. Spaces are counted
textFunction.leftExample: LEFT("Todayweatheris nice", 2)returns the two leftmost characters. The result is "Today"
textFunction.lenDescDtl: Counts the number of characters in text
textFunction.lenExample: LEN("Todayweatheris nice")counts characters in this text. The result is 7
textFunction.lowerDescDtl: Converts all uppercase letters in text to lowercase
textFunction.midDesc: Return characters from a specified position
textFunction.midDescDtl: Returns a specified number of characters from a specified position in text
textFunction.regexReplaceDesc: Replace text using a regular expression
textFunction.regexReplaceDescDtl: Matches and replaces text using a regular expression. Occurrence: 0 replaces all matches (default), a positive number replaces the Nth match from the beginning, and a negative number replaces the Nth match from the end. Case sensitivity: 0 is case-sensitive (default), and 1 is case-insensitive. When entering regex escapes such as \d directly in a formula, place them in the pattern string; these escapes are not currently supported inside string fragments assembled with functions. Error values: returns #VALUE when a required argument is missing, occurrence is not an integer, or case sensitivity is not 0 or 1; formula evaluation fails when the regular expression is invalid; returns the original text when no match is found.
textFunction.replaceDescDtl: Replaces part of the specified text with new text based on position and replacement length
textFunction.replaceSyntax: REPLACE(Text, Start Position, Replacement Length, New Text)
textFunction.reptDescDtl: Repeats text a specified number of times
textFunction.rightDesc: Return specified characters from the left
textFunction.rightDescDtl: Returns a specified number of characters from the right side of a text value. If the text is shorter, returns the original text. Spaces are counted
textFunction.rightExample: RIGHT("Todayweatheris nice", 2)returns the two rightmost characters. The result is "nice"
textFunction.rmbFmtDescDtl: Converts an amount number to uppercase RMB text
textFunction.rmbFmtExample: RMBFORMAT(16. 83)returns "RMB sixteen yuan, eight jiao, three fen"
textFunction.rmbFmtDescDtl2: Converts an amount number to uppercase RMB text
textFunction.rmbFmtExample2: RMBFORMAT(16. 83)returns "RMB sixteen yuan, eight jiao, three fen"
textFunction.searchDescDtl: Gets the start position of Text1 in Text2
textFunction.splitDescDtl: Splits text into an array by the specified delimiter
textFunction.trimDescDtl: Removes leading and trailing spaces from text
textFunction.trimExample: TRIM(" Todayweatheris nice ")has spaces at both ends, so after trimming, the result is "Todayweatheris nice"
textFunction.unionDescDtl: Merges multiple text values into an array and removes duplicates
textFunction.randCodeDescDtl: Generates a unique random code as a 32-character string made of numbers and letters

logicFunction.title: Logic Functions
logicFunction.andDescDtl: Checks whether all logical expressions are true. Returns true if yes, otherwise false
logicFunction.andSyntax: AND(Logical Expression1, Logical Expression2, ..., Logical ExpressionN)
logicFunction.andExample: AND(Number1>10, Number2>20)returns true if Number1 is greater than 10 and Number2 is greater than 20, otherwise false
logicFunction.ifDescDtl: Checks whether a condition is met. Returns one value if true and another value if false
logicFunction.ifSyntax: IF(logical expression, value if true, value if false)
logicFunction.ifExample: IF(Score>60, "Pass", "Fail"), When Score is greater than 60, returns "Pass", otherwise returns "Fail"
logicFunction.ifsDescDtl: Checks conditions in order. If the first condition is met, returns the first value; otherwise checks the second condition and returns the second value if met, and so on
logicFunction.ifsSyntax: IFS(Logical Expression1, Value1, Logical Expression2, Value2, ...)
logicFunction.ifsExample: IFS(Rating==5, "Excellent", Rating>=3, "Good", Rating==2, "Pass", Rating<=1, "Bad"), returns an evaluation based on the rating
logicFunction.isEmptyDescDtl: Checks whether a field is empty text, an empty object, or an empty array. Returns true if empty, otherwise false
logicFunction.isEmptyExample: ISEMPTY(Single Line), returns true when the Single Line field is empty
logicFunction.notDescDtl: Checks whether a condition is met. Returns false if met and true if not met
logicFunction.notExample: NOT(Score>60), returns false when Score is greater than 60, otherwise true
logicFunction.orDescDtl: Checks whether any logical expression is true. Returns true if yes, otherwise false
logicFunction.orSyntax: OR(Logical Expression1, Logical Expression2, ..., Logical ExpressionN)
logicFunction.orExample: OR(Rating1==5, Rating2==5, Rating3==5), returns true when any of the three ratings equals 5, and false when none equals 5
logicFunction.xorDescDtl: Returns XOR across all arguments. The result is true only when exactly one logical expression is true and the others are false
logicFunction.xorSyntax: XOR(Logical Expression1, Logical Expression2, ..., Logical ExpressionN)
logicFunction.xorExample: XOR(Chinese Score>90, Math Score>90), returns false if both scores are >90, false if both are <90, and true if one score is >90 and the other is <90
logicFunction.containsDescDtl: Checks whether arrays contain the specified element
logicFunction.containsExample: CONTAINS(Student Subform. Name, John), returns true if any row in the Student subform has Name equal to John, otherwise false
logicFunction.containsColDescDtl: Checks whether the full column of specified fields in a form contains the specified element
logicFunction.containsColExample: CONTAINSCOLUMN(Form Field1, Form Field2, Field N), returns true if the full column of Form Field1 contains the value of Field N, otherwise false
logicFunction.equalDescDtl: Checks whether arrays are all equal
logicFunction.equalExample: EQUAL(Student Subform. Name, John), returns true if every row in the Student subform has Name equal to John, otherwise false
logicFunction.equalColDescDtl: Checks whether the full column of specified fields in a form contains the specified element
logicFunction.equalColExample:
EQUALCOLUMN(Form Field1, Form Field2, Field N), when Field N is an array, returns true if each row of Form Field1, Form Field2, and Field N is equal, otherwise false;
when Field N is not an array, returns true if each row of Form Field1 and Form Field2 equals Field N, otherwise false
